newsitem.title: PERU: Cementos Lima to finance expansion with bonds.
newsitem.headline: Cementos Lima to finance expansion with bonds.

text.p: Peru's largest cement firm, Cementos Lima, plans to finance the second phase of its production plant expansion with a bond issue of up to $60 million.
"The second stage of the expansion work will start in early 1998 and will be financed by the corporate bonds approved by the company," said a company official who asked not to be named.
The firm's shareholders approved the bond issue last Friday. The company has not yet announced the date and details of the issue.

The Cementos official said the first stage of the production plant's expansion, at a cost of $130 million, was 90 percent complete. The first phase would raise annual capacity to 2.5 million tonnes from the current 1.7 million tonnes by the third quarter of 1997, he said.
"With the second stage, we are going to have a production capacity of between 3.6 million and 4.0 million tonnes of cement annually," he said.
Cementos Lima forecasts 1996 sales of $365 million, two percent higher than last year.
